checks.evidence: Independently verified frozen index tree, all 41 manifest hashes, every remote-only/local-only blob and sole shared reading-test union. No B/G1 source present.

25/25 runtime reading/music tests and scoped inherited-strict compiler exit0 are honest bounded checks, but none covers public collection read of stored owner credential. Critical access-control exposure is concrete in registered collection schema.
History can become a normal remote fast-forward, but source security blocker must be fixed/reviewed first. No force-push/deployment/DB/provider operation performed.

issues.issue: Registered Setlists collection permits anonymous read, while appleMusic.ownerUserToken is an ordinary text field without read access restriction. apple-token POST stores the MusicKit owner credential there. Standard Payload collection API reads can therefore disclose the stored owner token, bypassing the custom GET endpoint’s isConfigured-only projection.
issues.fix: Deny public/API field reads for ownerUserToken using a narrow field access restriction while retaining the existing authorized server/internal token write/sync path. Add a regression demonstrating credential field is not readable by ordinary/anonymous API readers; do not require actual credentials or provider/DB calls. Re-freeze changed candidate and rerun both fresh independent reviews.
issues.qualification: Existing upstream source discovered during integration, not a demonstrated configured/live leak. No real token accessed or rotation claimed; do not publish a known secret-access defect merely because upstream already contains it.

limitations: Source review only. No workloads, browser, DB, provider/network, source/index/registry edits, other assessment access or live acceptance. Parent retains actual commit/push verification gates.
